**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Catch the other `testzip()` failures so corrupt packages produce a clean error.**

`_validate_docx` turns only `BadZipFile` into `ValueError`. `ZipFile.testzip()` catches `BadZipFile` per member, and a CRC mismatch is reported through that path. Other read failures propagate unchanged:
- Corrupt deflate data in an entry raises `zlib.error`.
- An unsupported compression method raises `NotImplementedError`.
- An entry encrypted at the ZIP level raises `RuntimeError`.
- A truncated stream can raise `EOFError`.

The `create-comparison` handler in `cli.py` (Line 191) catches only `OSError` and `ValueError`. A damaged DOCX therefore ends with an uncaught traceback. The user does not get the `doc-lineage create-comparison: Corrupt DOCX package: ...` message.

No record is written, because validation runs before `mkdir`. Only the error contract breaks. Add a test that uses a package whose deflate stream is corrupted.

**🔒 Security & Privacy** | **🟡 Minor** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Create the record store and record files with owner-only permissions.**

`directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` and `open("x")` use the process umask. With the common umask `022`, the directory gets mode `0755` and each record gets mode `0644`. Each record holds absolute source paths. In the documented work library (one folder per manager, then one per document category), those paths show manager names and document categories. Other local users can then read them.

Set restrictive modes explicitly. Keep the exclusive-creation semantics.
